key_insight: LLMSurgeon formalizes Data Mixture Surgery (DMS) to recover domain-level mixtures of an LLM's pretraining corpus using only the model's generated text, enabling post-hoc inference of what kinds of data shaped the model.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of transparency about LLM pretraining data by estimating the composition (domain-level proportions) of a model's training mixture from its outputs alone, enabling provenance auditing and diagnosis of capability/failure sources.
method: Generate targeted prompts and model outputs to elicit domain-specific signals (probing diverse topics, styles, and factual cues).
Extract features/fingerprints from outputs (embeddings, classifier scores, topic distributions) and compare them to reference domain signatures.
Fit a mixture model (e.g., likelihood/EM or optimization over domain weights) to infer domain proportions and validate using synthetic or held-out mixtures.
impact: Enables practitioners and auditors to reconstruct coarse-grained training data composition for closed models, informing bias attribution, risk assessment, compliance, and dataset-driven mitigations without access to raw pretraining corpora.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: probe generation → feature extraction → mixture fitting → inferred domain proportions.
Pie chart of inferred domain mixture (percentages) to summarize the model's "digital DNA."
Bar chart comparing true vs. recovered mixtures for validation (or sensitivity across prompt sets).
Heatmap or matrix of domain attribution across probe types to show which prompts reveal which data sources.
paper_title: LLMSurgeon: Diagnosing Data Mixture of Large Language Models
paper_authors: Yaxin Luo, Jiacheng Cui, Xiaohan Zhao, Xinyi Shang, Jiacheng Liu
